## Reserve a face or fill a solid mask (`custom; solid`) {#sec-ch11-custom}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0
status: draft
-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
The custom callbacks do nothing; solid callbacks write literal ones into a ghost slab. Their meanings depend on the field supplied.
Default: off.
Order: exact discrete operation or local derivation below; coupled solver order not measured.
:::

### Derivation

No PDE discretization is introduced. The custom map is the identity on the supplied tensor. The solid
map replaces every ghost entry by one. Reapplying either map returns the same tensor, so both are idempotent.
For a Boolean mask, one denotes solid; for a hydro state vector it is merely the number one in every row and
is not a physical state construction. `custom_inner` ([`bc_func.cpp:7-8`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L7-L8)) and `solid_inner` ([`bc_func.cpp:68-87`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L68-L87)) define these
operations directly. C1 verifies identity and constant-one ghost fills without assuming a thermodynamic meaning.

The report-only checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`; their current output is
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

Custom keeps a non-null callback slot for a user or layout operation. Solid acts on all variables supplied
and skips collapsed axes. Rectification applies solid callbacks to its mask before the directional sweeps,
then optionally applies caller-supplied callbacks. No independent spatial accuracy order applies.

@fig-ch11-custom-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

: Implementation sites for custom. {#tbl-ch11-custom-code}

1. Leave the tensor unchanged for custom. The anchor `custom_inner` is in [`bc_func.cpp:7-8`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L7-L8).
2. For solid, assign one to the requested ghost slab. The anchor `solid_inner` is in [`bc_func.cpp:68-87`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L68-L87).
3. Use solid on a mask; do not infer a hydro wall from the function name. The anchor `rectify_solid` is in [`rectify_solid.cpp:109-168`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/rectify_solid.cpp#L109-L168).

### Limits

A custom no-op does not supply missing physical ghost data. A non-null custom face still passes the
physical-face predicate. Using solid on hydro writes literal ones; it does not construct a no-slip or
thermodynamic wall. Caller-supplied rectification callbacks must be callable; the loop does not guard null entries.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result is claimed.
